summary: Persistent remote-controlled agent exposes PTY shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade to WebSocket peer
details: The package runs as a long-lived agent that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (SERVER_URL / config) and dispatches server-sent messages to privileged sinks on the host. Handlers include terminal_input (writes remote bytes into a spawned login-shell PTY via term.pty.write), read_file / write_file (arbitrary filesystem read/write), git_* operations, and upgrade_agent (runs `npm view @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest version` and then `npm install "$PKG"` via a spawned upgrade script, followed by a systemd/launchctl/PM2 service restart). The self-upgrade path is unpinned and gated only by a message from the connected server. The service installer also modifies the user's shell PATH (service/linux.js appends ~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin, etc.). Any party that can send WebSocket frames to the configured server — including the server operator, an attacker who compromises that server, or an attacker who compromises the npm package/maintainer account and pushes a new @latest — obtains full-host remote code execution with the agent's privileges, plus persistence across restarts via the managed service.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
